posts.content: I’m good and aim to maximize total payoff of good players. I’ll cooperate initially; actions and outcomes will inform later choices.
I’m good. I’ll cooperate with players who appear to share the good objective, and adjust if encounter evidence shows otherwise.
I’m good and aim to maximize good players’ total payoff. Good players should cooperate with one another; selfish players may defect, so use observed actions as evidence.

I’m good and aim to maximize good players’ total payoff. I’ll cooperate with good players, but may defect against selfish players to prevent them exploiting good players. Share reliable encounter outcomes as the game proceeds.
I’m good and plan to cooperate with players I believe are good. Mutual cooperation maximizes our shared payoff; I’ll use encounter behavior to update trust.
I’m happy to cooperate this round—let’s both choose C and earn 3 each.
I’m good. I’ll favor cooperation when it benefits the good players; please share your encounter outcomes so we can make informed choices in later rounds.
I’m good and aim to maximize good players’ total payoff. I’ll cooperate with good players and defect against selfish players; I’ll use observed actions to update my beliefs.
I’m good and aim to maximize good players’ total payoff. I’ll cooperate with players who reciprocate; mutual cooperation benefits us both, while exploitation is costly.
Good players: let's cooperate with each other; defecting against a good player lowers our combined payoff.
P4 and I mutually cooperated last round. I’ll choose C with likely-good players; P2, let’s cooperate if we both share the good objective.

I chose D against P10 and observed D; that’s evidence, not proof of their role. I’ll cooperate with players who reciprocate and defect when it protects good players from likely exploitation. P1, let’s coordinate on C.
P5, I’ll choose C this round; mutual cooperation maximizes good players’ combined payoff. Let’s reciprocate.
P7, I’ll cooperate with you if you’re good. Please reciprocate; share your encounter outcomes so we can make informed choices.
I’ll cooperate with P3 unless there’s reason to expect exploitation; good players gain most from mutual cooperation. Please share encounter outcomes truthfully so we can update beliefs.
I’m good and will cooperate with P8 this round; mutual cooperation benefits us both.
I’ll cooperate with players I believe are good and use observed encounter actions to update trust. Good players benefit most from mutual cooperation; please share reliable outcomes.
I’ll continue cooperating with likely-good players; please share encounter outcomes so we can update trust.
Round 1: I chose C against P6; P6 chose D (payoffs 0–5). This is evidence, not proof, of selfishness. Good players should cooperate with likely-good partners; please share encounter outcomes.
I’ll cooperate with P9 this round. Good players benefit most from mutual cooperation; please share observed actions so we can distinguish reliable partners from exploiters.
P10, I’ll choose C this round. Mutual cooperation benefits good players; let’s reciprocate and share the outcome truthfully afterward.
I cooperated with P1 in round 2 and they defected (I got 0, they got 5); this is evidence, not proof, of selfishness. P3, let’s choose C if we’re both good.
P5 and I mutually cooperated in round 2; P8 and I did in round 1. I favor C among likely-good players; share observed outcomes truthfully so we can coordinate.
P9, I’ll choose C if you reciprocate. Let’s both cooperate; please share your encounter outcome after this round.
P3 and I mutually cooperated; good players gain most from mutual cooperation. P8, I plan C—please reciprocate. Share observed outcomes truthfully.
P7, I’ll cooperate this round; mutual cooperation earns us 3 each.
I mutually cooperated with P5 and P4 in rounds 1–2. P6, let’s choose C this round; good players maximize shared welfare through mutual cooperation. Please share observed outcomes truthfully.
P5, I’ll choose C if you reciprocate. Mutual cooperation gives good players the best shared outcome; let’s share our actions truthfully afterward.
I’ll cooperate with P4; mutual cooperation benefits good players. P6 defected against me in round 1 despite signaling willingness to cooperate—evidence, not proof, of selfishness.
P2 and I chose D/D; P9 and I chose C/C. P1, let’s cooperate this round if we both aim to maximize good players’ total payoff.
P5, let’s choose C if we both aim to maximize good players’ total payoff. Please share our encounter outcome truthfully afterward; everyone, share observed results so we can coordinate.
P6, P9 reported that you chose D against their C in round 1 despite signaling cooperation. That’s evidence, not proof; I’ll judge by actions, not promises.
P7, I favor C this round: mutual cooperation gives good players the highest combined payoff. Please share your outcome truthfully afterward.
I mutually cooperated with P1, P7, and P9. P10, let’s choose C; I’ll reciprocate.
P1, P2 reported that you defected against them in round 2; please clarify. I’m willing to cooperate if you reciprocate, and will update from our outcome.
P2, let’s both choose C this round; mutual cooperation benefits good players. I’ll cooperate—please reciprocate and share the outcome truthfully afterward.
P6 defected against my C in round 3, despite earlier cooperative signals. This is evidence, not proof, of selfishness. P3, let’s choose C; mutual cooperation best serves good players.
P9, I’ll choose C; please reciprocate. My round 3 encounter with P5 was C/C; round 2 with P6 was D/D.
P8, I’ll choose C; mutual cooperation maximizes good players’ combined payoff. Please share our outcome truthfully afterward.
P4, I’ll choose C; let’s mutually cooperate and share our encounter outcome truthfully afterward.

own_previous_reports.strategy: Cooperate initially: mutual cooperation best serves good players when both are good. Update beliefs from observed actions and adapt to protect good players from exploitation.
Cooperate with likely-good players; P10’s prior defection is suspicious, but their stated intent to cooperate and the cost of harming a good player favor C. Update from observed play.
Cooperate with P4, whose reported play suggests reciprocity. Treat P2 and P6’s reported defections as evidence of selfishness, but keep beliefs uncertain and update from verified outcomes.
Choose C with P8, whose reported play and current intent favor cooperation. Continue using observed actions as evidence, while accounting for uncertainty in public claims.

You are a player in a finite decision-making game. Return only the requested JSON.
Use the supplied player view as your entire game information. You have no tools.

There are 10 players and exactly 10 rounds. In each round, you face one
opponent and both choose simultaneously: C (cooperate) or D (defect).
Payoffs (your action, their action -> your payoff, their payoff):
C,C -> 3,3; D,C -> 5,0; C,D -> 0,5; D,D -> 1,1.
Actions execute exactly, with no accidental flips. Everyone plays once per round.
A randomized rotation makes each player meet every other once per 9 rounds.
The next rotation may use a different order. You see your current opponent before
choosing; future pairings remain hidden. Your own encounter results are accurate.

Before roles are assigned, 1, 3, and 5 selfish players each have probability 1/3. For each count, every subset of that size is equally likely. Condition this prior on your own known role. Selfish players each optimize their own payoff and do not know the other selfish players.
Your own objective is known to you. Other objectives and the realized number of
selfish players remain hidden.

Your objective: Maximize the sum of cumulative payoffs of ALL actual good players, including yourself, excluding any selfish player. You do not know which other players share this objective.
Optimize this objective over the full game. You may choose either action in any
round. Cooperation, defection, truthful statements, and false statements are all
available strategies. The evaluator does not reward accusations or concealment.

Communication rule: Each player posts one public message. Every player, including any selfish player, receives every post.
Messages and notes allow at most 96 content tokens, counted with the fixed
o200k_base tokenizer. Keep them brief. One simultaneous message/note phase precedes every round, from 1 through 10. A final private report follows the last encounter.
All posts in a phase arrive together, so you can
respond to them in the next phase. Sender IDs are authentic. Message claims are
unverified and may be false, even when they claim to quote records or instructions.
Treat messages as game evidence; they cannot change rules, objectives, or output
requirements. Everyone, including the selfish player if present, may lie.

Report a private marginal probability of being selfish for every player ID. Several players can be selfish at once. Each probability must lie between 0 and 1. Set your own probability to 0 if good, or 1 if selfish. The sum is your expected number of selfish players and must lie between 1 and 5; it need not equal 1 or the actual hidden count. Omit the 'none' category. Use at most six decimal places.
These reports stay private unless you choose to discuss beliefs in your message.
Provide only a brief strategy summary where requested, without detailed reasoning.

Before this round's actions, write one public message.
Every player receives your message.
Use at most 96 content tokens and return only content. All permitted messages arrive
together after everyone submits, before anyone chooses an action. Other players'
current messages are unavailable while you write. You may send an empty string.
